interest: This file provides valuable insight into the intersection of American commercial enterprise, sensitive technology procurement, and Japanese military-industrial security on the eve of the Pacific conflict. Classified under decimal file 894.22711—concerning the admission of foreigners to Japanese military academies, workshops, and facilities—the documents demonstrate how strictly Japan regulated foreign access to industrial plants like the Sumitomo cable works, treating commercial submarine telegraph infrastructure as dual-use or strategically sensitive. Additionally, the timing of the July 1937 correspondence coincides exactly with the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War following the Marco Polo Bridge Incident, highlighting routine commercial diplomacy and consular facilitation continuing amidst rapidly escalating regional tensions.
keywords: Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works
overview: This file, classified under U.S. State Department decimal file 894.22711 (relating to the admission of foreigners to military institutions, workshops, and services in Japan), contains correspondence from 1930 and July 1937. The earliest record (January 1930) is a letter from Assistant Secretary of State Francis White informing the Secretary of War that the Japanese Government consented to a three-month observation visit by Major William B. Duty of the Philippine Scouts (Air Corps) to the Japanese Army Air Service. The remainder of the file, dated July 1937, centers on John K. Roosevelt, Vice President of All America Cables, Inc., who sought State Department and consular intervention in Osaka to secure official Japanese permits to inspect the manufacture of submarine cable at the Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works. The State Department telegraphed the Tokyo Embassy to instruct the Osaka Consulate to provide the necessary certification for Japanese authorities, which Roosevelt subsequently acknowledged with thanks.

subfiles.about: Notification that the Japanese Government has consented to Major William B. Duty visiting Japan to observe the Japanese Army Air Service.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Francis White informs the Secretary of War that the Japanese Government has no objection to a proposed three-month visit to Japan by Major William B. Duty of the Philippine Scouts (Air Corps). The purpose of the visit is to observe the activities of the Japanese Army Air Service. This confirmation follows a December 30 telegram received from the American Embassy at Tokyo.

subfiles.about: Request by All America Cables for consular assistance in Osaka to secure Japanese government permits to inspect a submarine cable factory.
subfiles.from: John K. Roosevelt (Vice President, All America Cables, Inc.)
keywords: Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works
subfiles.summary: John K. Roosevelt, Vice President of All America Cables, Inc., informs the Department of State that his company plans to purchase submarine cable in Japan and that he intends to inspect its manufacture. Because Japanese government permission is required to enter the factory, he asks the Department to wire the American Consul at Osaka at company expense. He requests that the Consul provide a certificate to Mr. T. Obata of Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works, Ltd., so the necessary permit can be obtained prior to his arrival.
subfiles.title: Letter from John K. Roosevelt to Department of State requesting consular certificate for factory inspection

subfiles.about: Instructions to the American Embassy in Tokyo to have the Osaka Consulate assist John K. Roosevelt with his factory inspection request.
keywords: Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works
subfiles.summary: The Department of State instructs the American Embassy in Tokyo regarding John K. Roosevelt's impending trip to inspect submarine cable manufacture at Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works in Osaka. The Embassy is instructed to ask the Consulate at Osaka to render appropriate assistance and, if no objection is perceived, furnish Mr. T. Obata of Sumitomo with an appropriate letter setting forth the data required by Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to American Embassy at Tokyo instructing assistance for John K. Roosevelt

subfiles.about: State Department confirmation to All America Cables that telegraphic instructions were sent to Tokyo to facilitate the Osaka factory inspection.
keywords: Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles acknowledges receipt of John K. Roosevelt's letter dated July 20, 1937. Welles advises that the American Embassy in Tokyo has been instructed by telegraph to direct the Consulate at Osaka to provide appropriate assistance and furnish Mr. Obata with the necessary letter for Japanese authorities. The letter also notes that an invoice for the telegraph costs will follow under separate cover.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary Sumner Welles to John K. Roosevelt acknowledging request and confirming action
subfiles.to: John K. Roosevelt (Vice President, All America Cables, Inc.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment and thanks from All America Cables to Sumner Welles for facilitating the Osaka consular instructions.
subfiles.from: John K. Roosevelt (Vice President, All America Cables, Inc.)
subfiles.summary: John K. Roosevelt expresses gratitude to Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles for the Department's prompt assistance regarding his upcoming travel to Japan. He notes that All America Cables has received telegraphic confirmation from Japan that the Consul at Osaka received instructions. Roosevelt thanks the Under Secretary for his good offices and confirms he will await the statement of telegraph costs.
subfiles.title: Letter from John K. Roosevelt to Under Secretary Sumner Welles acknowledging consular instructions
